hook.title: The pessimistic auditor
hook.text: You can't count the money in the vault ($\log p(x)$ is intractable). But an auditor can always certify *at least* some amount: the **evidence lower bound**. Any guess $q$ about how the vault is organised gives a valid certificate; a smarter guess raises the certified amount. The leftover gap between the true amount and the certificate is exactly how far off your guess $q$ is from the truth: $D_{KL}(q\|p(z|x))$. A perfect guess closes the gap completely.
hook.recall: Remember the auditor: ELBO is a guaranteed lower bound for any $q$; the slack equals $D_{KL}(q\|p(z|x))$, so it is tight exactly when $q$ is the true posterior.

explore.intro: A toy model with four latent values. You set $q(z)$; the page computes both ELBO decompositions and the gap.
tasks: Press **q = prior**, then **q = true posterior**. Watch the gap.
Try q concentrated on $z=1$ only. Why is it already close?
explore.takeaway: $\log p(x)=\text{ELBO}+D_{KL}(q\|p(z|x))$; ELBO $=\mathbb E_q[\log p(x|z)]-D_{KL}(q\|p(z))$; equality iff $q=p(z|x;\theta)$.

build.prompt: Order the derivation of the ELBO.
items: Apply Jensen: $\ge\mathbb E_q[\log p(z,x;\theta)-\log q(z)]=\mathcal L$
build.explanation: Slides 47–49 and 31–32: Jensen's inequality gives the bound for any $q$; splitting the joint gives the autoencoder form.

questions.prompt: The ELBO is a lower bound on $\log p(x;\theta)$ because of:
questions.explanation: The log is concave, so the log of an average is at least the average of the logs.

questions.prompt: $\mathbb E_q[\log p(x|z)]=-2.0$ and $D_{KL}(q\|p(z))=0.8$. What is the ELBO?

options: The ELBO holds for any distribution $q$
Maximising the ELBO over $\theta,\phi$ pushes up the log-likelihood
questions.explanation: KL is $\ge0$ (W2 slide 33). That’s precisely why the ELBO never exceeds $\log p(x)$.

questions.prompt: In the autoencoder form, which term plays the role of the *reconstruction* objective?
questions.explanation: First term: $\hat x\approx x_i$ (autoencoding loss). Second term pulls $q$ toward the prior.

questions.prompt: *“By Jensen, $\log\mathbb E_q[f]\le\mathbb E_q[\log f]$, so the ELBO is an **upper** bound on $\log p(x)$.”* Where is the mistake?
options: For the concave log, $\log\mathbb E[f]\ge\mathbb E[\log f]$: the inequality is reversed, so the ELBO is a **lower** bound
questions.explanation: The auditor certifies *at least*; an upper bound would be a different (and unsafe) certificate.
